claims.text: The baseline consists of equiatomic nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution nanoparticles with uniform elemental distribution.
The baseline particles have a typical HEA d-band structure.
Rh content can be increased relative to the other elements while retaining the PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution structure.
Increasing Rh content shifts the local d-band centers at Pt and Pd sites.
Composition-dependent electronic interactions tune adsorption energies of ethanol and oxygenated intermediates.
Rh-induced d-band shifts enhance chemisorption and activation of oxygenated intermediates during ethanol oxidation.
IrOsPtPdRhRu can catalyze ethanol oxidation through a 12-electron process.
Single-metal catalysts generally promote no more than a four-electron ethanol-oxidation process.
Increasing Rh content drives ethanol oxidation toward the 12-electron pathway rather than a four-electron pathway.
The proposed electronic tuning stabilizes intermediates that otherwise require higher overpotentials on monometallic surfaces.
The Rh-enriched catalyst will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential than the equiatomic baseline.
The Rh-enriched catalyst will produce higher ethanol-oxidation current density than the equiatomic baseline.
The Rh-enriched catalyst will show greater selectivity toward complete ethanol-oxidation products than the equiatomic baseline.
The electronic activation mechanism should operate in alkaline electrolyte at moderate temperatures while the catalyst remains a solid solution and avoids substantial sintering or phase separation.
A lack of statistically significant onset-potential or current-density improvement, or a lack of a corresponding d-band-center shift, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
